The prompt's setup line `python3 -c "import fitz" || pip install --quiet pymupdf` installs into /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages, but `python3` on this image is 3.11 and reads /usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages, so `import fitz` still failed after a 'successful' install. Consequences, all measured: scan.py printed 'scan SELFTEST FAIL - OCCL 30-Sep-2026 anti-dumping duty raise, generic subject: got []' because it could not read the PDF behind a generic heading; minsteel.py died on ModuleNotFoundError; india_spot's fuel and moil sources failed with 'No module named fitz'; and - the nastier part - orderbook.pdf_text CACHED THE FAILED READ AS AN EMPTY TEXT FILE, so the selftest kept failing even after the import was fixed. Fix: `python3 -m pip install pymupdf xlrd`, then delete the one 0-byte file under scripts/ideas/_cache/ob_text. After that scan.py printed SELFTEST PASS and was RE-RUN FROM SCRATCH, so the committed scan file is the one with PDF-text classification working; india_spot was re-run too and moil then returned 3 rows. For the owner: the setup line in the routine prompt should be `python3 -m pip install --quiet pymupdf xlrd`, otherwise every cloud run silently loses PDF text.

govt_considered.theme: critical_minerals - Critical minerals (lithium, nickel, cobalt): mining, processing, recycling
govt_considered.verdict: KEPT BY THE GATE, DECLINED FOR A CARD, AND THE EARLIER 'THE LANE DID NOT RUN' NOTE IN THIS LOG IS CORRECTED. The lane DID run - on the ideas-feeds Action at 18:56 IST, which read PIB and recorded scanned 37, opened 3, kept 1, dropped {no decision verb 29, noise 4, too small 2, duplicate 1, backgrounder 0, no theme 0}. This sandbox cannot reach pib.gov.in, so govt.py here reported the day unread; that was true of the sandbox, not of the day, and the Action's file is the one committed. WHY IT IS NOT A CARD. (1) It is a PIB BACKGROUNDER on a decision this page already considered and declined YESTERDAY: govt.json's own history line for the theme reads 'The 2026-11-04 capex scheme (Rs 2,814 cr) funds only four plants (2 lithium >=30 kt, 2 nickel >=50 kt), picked by the LOWEST subsidy bid; no company has filed that it will bid.' A backgrounder restating a scheme is not a new decision. (2) The theme has NO MEASURED BASKET HISTORY - theme_map.json's critical_minerals entry says so in as many words - so the government lane's central test, whether money becomes somebody's order book, has no evidence behind it here. (3) The structure argues against it: four plants awarded on the lowest subsidy bid is a narrow, winner-take-few programme, closer in shape to a household subsidy than to a procurement pipeline. (4) Not one mapped company has said it will bid. Every `why` line in govt.json ends with the same sentence, written by an earlier session: '(NSE filing summaries read 2026-11-04; the company has NOT said it will bid for the 2026-11-04 scheme)'. THE MAPPED NAMES IN THE Rs 200-7,500 cr BAND, for the record and not as a recommendation: Mishra Dhatu Nigam (MIDHANI, Rs 6,986 cr, 1 own filing - MoU with Heavy Water Board and BARC for nickel and cobalt recovery from plant reverts, 27-Oct-2026); Sindhu Trade Links (SINDHUTRAD, Rs 3,755 cr, 1 own filing - board approved a long-term strategy to invest in critical minerals, 10-Jul-2025); Neogen Chemicals (NEOGEN, Rs 6,547 cr, 1 own filing - doubling organo-lithium capacity from 300 to 600 MT/PA at Patancheru, 31-Oct-2026, which is downstream lithium chemistry, NOT ore processing). Each has exactly ONE filing of its own touching the theme. The larger mapped names (Oil India, Vedanta, Hindustan Zinc) are far above the band. WHAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED HERE, SAID PLAINLY: the Rs 10,000 crore outlay is recorded in govt.json as coming from the release BODY ('amount_in': 'body'), and govt.json does not store the body text. pib.gov.in is refused at this sandbox's egress proxy, so THE RELEASE ITSELF WAS NOT OPENED IN THIS RUN and the Rs 10,000 cr figure, its period and what it covers are UNKNOWN beyond the builder's extraction. That alone would stop a card being published on it. No company was added to or removed from theme_map.json: critical_minerals already exists with 13 companies and the release is mapped, so there was no unmapped-release research to do.

researched.name: Highway Infrastructure Ltd
researched.reason: The order-book jump is real and confirmed from both ends in the companies' own documents (Rs 1,776.19 cr at 31-Oct-2026 against Rs 775 cr at 30-Sep-2025), and the business is genuinely scaling - Q1 FY27 total income Rs 304.3 cr against Rs 112.5 cr. The research is published at LOW confidence because everything underneath the headline points the other way. EBITDA margin fell to 1.6% from 10.7% as toll traffic at Moti Naroli and other plazas undershot the fixed licence fees the company had bid. FY26 profit growth is an accounting entry: the standalone P&L carries a separate line 'Gain on Re-measurement of Inventory upon conversion into Investment Property Rs 19,78,96,713', so stripping it takes FY26 PAT from Rs 32.10 cr to about Rs 12.3 cr - BELOW FY25's Rs 19.66 cr - and Infomerics' own adjusted net cash accrual of Rs 14.36 cr says the same thing from the cash side. On TTM earnings excluding that one-off the stock is on about 83x. Add promoter warrants priced 31% below market (1 cr warrants at Rs 49.82, relevant date 14-Oct-2026, EGM 13-Nov), a related-party purchase of 51% of a nil-turnover company from directors' relatives, Brickwork keeping the issuer in 'Issuer Not Cooperating' since 6-Jun-2026, 15 order filings in 240 days (the measured serial-bidder bucket, 17.3% odds of a 2x and never a 5x), and Group T settlement with Rs 5-7 lakh of daily turnover. Published because the jump is confirmed and the reader deserves the full picture; low confidence because nothing yet shows the book becoming cash profit.

researched.reason: Top of the scan at score 16 on a day of 52 candidates, with five filings at once: H1 FY27 results (revenue Rs 549.71 cr +60.67%, PAT Rs 22.12 cr +37.82%), an earnings release, an investor presentation, a Reg 32 deviation statement and an RMC-plant intimation. THE RESEARCH CHANGED THE HEADLINE. The release says the order book is 'up 42% from Rs 1,235 Cr in Mar 2026' to Rs 1,755.06 cr - true, and measured from a trough. An X post relaying an older filing pointed at the company's OWN press release of 16-Oct-2025, which this run then fetched from BSE and read: the unexecuted order book was Rs 1,534.60 cr at 30-Sep-2025. Year on year the book is therefore up 14.4%, not 42%, and it FELL 19.5% between September 2025 and March 2026. Both releases give segment splits, so the mix change is measurable too: EPC-Road 997.56 -> 589.03 (-41%) while toll collection went 275.00 -> 962.00 (+250%). The company is migrating from building things to collecting tolls on a gross-revenue basis, which is exactly what the 165 bps of EBITDA margin it gave up in H1 looks like. Published anyway, at medium confidence: 9.3x trailing and 8-11x forward earnings, 18% FY26 ROE, debt/equity 0.27 and operating cash flow positive again, which is cheaper than every main-board road EPC comparable priced in this run. Red flags written onto the card: directors' remuneration approved above the Section 197 cap with the amounts not disclosed, promoter warrants at Rs 119 against a Rs 195.5 close, a Rs 2.5 cr unsecured ICD at 12%, and the deck quoting three different H1 FY27 revenue figures.

data_problems: *** THE ROUTINE'S OWN SETUP LINE INSTALLS PyMuPDF INTO THE WRONG PYTHON, AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND CACHED. The prompt's step 0 runs `python3 -c "import fitz" || pip install --quiet pymupdf`. On this image `pip` writes to /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages while `python3` is 3.11 and reads /usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages, so the install 'succeeds' and the import still fails. Measured consequences before it was caught: scan.py printed 'scan SELFTEST FAIL - OCCL 30-Sep-2026 anti-dumping duty raise, generic subject: got []' (it cannot classify a generic heading without PDF text, which is the exact 43%-in-three-weeks miss the selftest exists to prevent); minsteel.py died with ModuleNotFoundError; india_spot's fuel and moil sources failed the same way. WORSE: orderbook.pdf_text writes its result to scripts/ideas/_cache/ob_text EVEN WHEN THE EXTRACTION FAILED, so the empty string was cached and the selftest kept failing after the import was fixed. FIX APPLIED HERE: `python3 -m pip install pymupdf xlrd`, then delete the 0-byte file under scripts/ideas/_cache/ob_text; scan.py then printed SELFTEST PASS and was re-run from scratch. FOR THE OWNER: change the routine prompt's setup line to `python3 -m pip install --quiet pymupdf xlrd`, and consider not caching an empty pdf_text result (scripts/ideas/orderbook.py line ~213) so a transient reader failure cannot poison the cache.
